found.lens: Quantum chemistry / molecular spectroscopy: electronic-structure integral conventions, molecular electric moments and response tensors, rovibrational effective Hamiltonians, radiative-transition coefficient definitions, transition-state-theory statistical prefactors, and system–bath models. In this literature most of the damage is done by dimensionless combinatorial factors, by same-symbol-different-operational-definition parameters, and by definitions whose variants differ in *dimension* (so a lint reports an "error" where there is only a convention).

gaps.name: Einstein B-coefficient radiation-field basis (ρ_ν vs ρ_ω vs ρ_ν̃ vs mean intensity J̄_ν)
gaps.what_breaks: Every paper writes the same equation dN/dt = B ρ N and the same phrase "Einstein B coefficient", but B is defined against at least four different measures of the field, two of which have different DIMENSIONS. Per spectral energy density, [B_ρ] = m³ J⁻¹ s⁻² ; per mean intensity, [B_J] = m² sr J⁻¹ s⁻¹ — they differ by a velocity, exactly c/4π. A dimensional solve that has one variant in its registry will declare the other paper dimensionally inconsistent, or will 'restore' a spurious c to make it balance. Dimensional analysis cannot see the ν↔ν̃ and ν↔ω variants at all, since those are pure factors of c and 2π on an already-consistent equation.
gaps.magnitude: B_J = (4π/c)·B_ρ (4π/c = 4.19×10⁻¹⁰ s m⁻¹); per-wavenumber vs per-frequency multiplies by c; per-angular-frequency vs per-frequency multiplies by 2π. Compounded, up to c·2π/4π ≈ 1.5×10¹⁰ between two literally-labelled "B₂₁" values.
gaps.example: Variant A (energy-density basis, Einstein 1917 / most physical-chemistry texts): A₂₁ = (8πhν³/c³) B₂₁, B₂₁ in m³ J⁻¹ s⁻². Variant B (mean-intensity basis, radiative-transfer and astrochemistry, e.g. LAMDA/RADEX): A₂₁ = (2hν³/c²) B₂₁, B₂₁ in m² sr J⁻¹ s⁻¹. Variant C (wavenumber basis, HITRAN-adjacent line lists): A₂₁ = 8πhc ν̃³ B₂₁.
gaps.fingerprint: Read the A–B relation the paper prints and key off which of {8πhν³/c³, 2hν³/c², 8πhcν̃³, ħω³/π²c³} appears; cross-check against the stated units of B (m³ J⁻¹ s⁻² vs m² J⁻¹ s⁻¹ vs cm³ erg⁻¹ s⁻²) and against whether the field variable is ρ_ν/u_ν, J̄_ν (mean intensity), or I_ν. Presence of the symbol J̄ or the operator (1/4π)∫dΩ is decisive for the intensity basis.

gaps.name: Two-electron integral index pairing: chemists' (Mulliken) vs physicists' (Dirac) vs antisymmetrized notation
gaps.what_breaks: (pq|rs), ⟨pq|rs⟩ and ⟨pq||rs⟩ are the same rank-4 tensor read with different index pairings: (pq|rs) = ⟨pr|qs⟩, and ⟨pq||rs⟩ = ⟨pq|rs⟩ − ⟨pq|sr⟩. All variants are energies (E_h) with identical dimensions, so a dimensional lint is blind, yet a mis-pairing silently exchanges a Coulomb integral for an exchange integral in any Fock-matrix, MP2, or coupled-cluster expression the tool tries to parse or re-emit. The double-bar form additionally hides a subtraction, so 'the integral' is not a single object at all.
gaps.magnitude: Not a scalar factor — an index permutation (J ↔ K swap) plus, for the double-bar form, a hidden difference of two terms. Physically Coulomb and exchange integrals over the same orbital pair routinely differ by an order of magnitude and the exchange term carries the opposite sign in the energy expression, so the induced error is O(1) in the total, not a small correction.
gaps.example: Mulliken/chemists': F_μν = h_μν + Σ_λσ P_λσ[(μν|λσ) − ½(μλ|νσ)]. Dirac/physicists' spin-orbital form of the same object: f_pq = h_pq + Σ_i ⟨pi||qi⟩ = h_pq + Σ_i (⟨pi|qi⟩ − ⟨pi|iq⟩). The strings '(μν|λσ)' and '⟨μν|λσ⟩' name different integrals despite identical index order.
gaps.fingerprint: Bracket glyph and bar count: round-with-bar (pq|rs) or [pq|rs] ⇒ Mulliken; angle-with-single-bar ⟨pq|rs⟩ ⇒ Dirac; angle-with-double-bar ⟨pq||rs⟩ ⇒ antisymmetrized. Corroborate with the Fock/energy expression printed: the '−½' Mulliken exchange prefactor vs the double-bar form, and with an explicit '(chemists'/physicists' notation)' statement, which most electronic-structure papers give once in Sec. II.

gaps.name: Molecular multipole moment definition: Buckingham ½-traceless Θ vs untraced second moment vs unhalved Q
gaps.what_breaks: 'The quadrupole moment' names at least three different tensors. Buckingham/IUPAC: Θ_αβ = ½Σ q_i(3r_αr_β − r²δ_αβ). Nuclear-physics-style and several QC codes: Q_αβ = Σ q_i(3r_αr_β − r²δ_αβ) (no ½). Gaussian and others also print the primitive second moment M_αβ = Σ q_i r_αr_β. All three have identical dimensions (charge×length²) and identical unit labels (D·Å, buckingham, ea₀², esu·cm²), so the tool cannot separate a factor-2 convention change from a genuine value difference, and the trace subtraction is not even a scalar factor — it can flip the sign of a component.
gaps.magnitude: Factor 2 between Θ and Q; between traceless and primitive, Θ_zz = (3/2)M_zz − ½(M_xx+M_yy+M_zz), a component-dependent affine map that can change sign. Unit-conversion edges also needed: 1 buckingham = 1 D·Å = 10⁻²⁶ esu cm² = 3.3356×10⁻⁴⁰ C m²; 1 ea₀² = 4.4866×10⁻⁴⁰ C m² = 1.3450 D·Å.
gaps.example: CO₂: Θ_zz = −4.3 D·Å (Buckingham ½ convention, the value quoted in essentially all intermolecular-forces work) vs Q_zz = −8.6 D·Å if the same charge distribution is reported in the unhalved convention, vs a set of primitive second moments M_xx = M_yy ≠ M_zz whose z component is large and positive.
gaps.fingerprint: Look for the explicit ½ in front of the (3r_αr_β − r²δ_αβ) kernel; for the presence of the −r²δ_αβ term at all (absent ⇒ primitive second moment); for the word 'traceless'/'primitive'; for the unit token 'buckingham' (which is tied to the Buckingham convention by name but not enforced); and for the code banner (ORCA/Gaussian/Dalton each print a distinct set).

gaps.name: Molecular response tensors α, β, γ: order-dependent (4πε₀) rider and polarizability-as-volume
gaps.what_breaks: The tool's E&M rider table covers the field variables (B, A, H, M, D) and the linear susceptibility (χ_SI = 4πχ_cgs), but molecular response tensors need a per-symbol rider whose 4πε₀ exponent grows with the tensor order, and half of them change dimension between systems. In esu/'polarizability volume' conventions α is literally a volume (Å³ or cm³); in SI it is C² m² J⁻¹. A dimensional solve on μ = αE therefore fails outright against an esu-convention paper — and 'fixing' it by restoring ε₀ silently changes β and γ by the wrong power.
gaps.magnitude: SI value = (4πε₀)^{(n+1)/2} × cgs value for the n-th order response (α: (4πε₀)¹; β: (4πε₀)^{3/2} — a half-integer exponent the engine already supports; γ: (4πε₀)²). Numerically: 1 a.u. of α = 0.1481847 Å³ = 1.648777×10⁻⁴¹ C² m² J⁻¹; 1 a.u. of β = 8.6392×10⁻³³ esu = 3.206361×10⁻⁵³ C³ m³ J⁻²; 1 a.u. of γ = 5.0367×10⁻⁴⁰ esu = 6.235380×10⁻⁶⁵ C⁴ m⁴ J⁻³. Getting the exponent wrong by one is a factor 1.11×10⁻¹⁰ (or its inverse).
gaps.example: Gaussian-system/'polarizability volume': α(H₂O) = 1.45 Å³, with μ = αE and E in statvolt cm⁻¹. SI: α(H₂O) = 1.61×10⁻⁴⁰ C² m² J⁻¹ = 4πε₀ × 1.45×10⁻³⁰ m³. Same symbol, same equation, dimensions L³ vs M⁻¹L⁻²T⁴I².
gaps.fingerprint: α quoted in Å³, cm³, or described as 'polarizability volume'; β/γ quoted 'in esu' or '×10⁻³⁰ esu'; absence of ε₀ from the defining relation μ = αE + ½βE² + ⅙γE³; or explicit 'atomic units' with a₀³-scale numbers. The tensor order is read off the power of E in the expansion the paper prints.

gaps.name: Suppressed standard-state divisor inside transcendental functions, and the co-transform of fitted intercepts
gaps.what_breaks: Chemical kinetics and thermodynamics write ln k, ln K_c, ln a, log₁₀ P with the reference quantity divided out by convention rather than in print. A lint that requires dimensionless arguments produces a false positive on essentially every Arrhenius, van 't Hoff, Eyring, and Antoine equation in the literature. The converse failure is worse: when the tool converts the units of the argument, the *fitted intercept* must shift by the log of the conversion factor while the slope is invariant — a unit converter that transforms k but leaves ln A (or the Antoine A) alone produces an internally inconsistent equation that still passes every dimensional check. This is distinct from the logarithmic-unit refuse class (dB, dex, pH): here the quantity is linear and fully convertible, only the reference is elided.
gaps.magnitude: Intercept shift = ln(conversion factor). Converting a bimolecular rate constant from cm³ molecule⁻¹ s⁻¹ to L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹ multiplies by N_A/1000 = 6.0221×10²⁰, so ln A shifts by 47.85 and log₁₀ A by 20.78. For Antoine, switching P from mmHg to bar shifts A by log₁₀(750.06) = 2.875 — and switching T from °C to K also moves C by 273.15, which the affine refuse class must be told to expect inside a fitted correlation.
gaps.example: Variant A: ln k = ln A − E_a/RT with A = 1.0×10⁻¹⁰ cm³ molecule⁻¹ s⁻¹. Variant B, same reaction: ln k = ln A − E_a/RT with A = 6.02×10¹⁰ L mol⁻¹ s⁻¹. Antoine: log₁₀ P[bar] = 4.6543 − 1435.264/(T[K] − 64.848) vs log₁₀ P[mmHg] = 8.07131 − 1730.63/(T[°C] + 233.426), both printed as 'the Antoine equation for water'.
gaps.fingerprint: A transcendental function whose argument the dimensional solve finds dimensionful, where the argument is a concentration, pressure, rate constant, equilibrium constant, or activity; or an equation of the recognized Arrhenius / van 't Hoff / Eyring / Antoine / Clausius–Clapeyron shape; or a fitted parameter tabulated as 'log A' with units attached to A elsewhere in the same table.

gaps.name: Bath spectral-density and reorganization-energy normalization in system–bath models
gaps.what_breaks: J(ω) in spin-boson / Redfield / HEOM / Marcus work is defined from microscopic couplings with a convention-dependent π, and 'reorganization energy' is used for both λ and the Stokes shift 2λ. Both J and λ carry energy-related dimensions in every convention, so nothing dimensional flags the mismatch; the tool would happily translate ħω units while the physical coupling strength is off by π or 2. This is not the one-sided/two-sided PSD question of a measured signal: J is defined by a sum over discrete oscillator couplings, and the fork is in that defining sum.
gaps.magnitude: Factor π/2 in the definition of J from {c_k}; factor 2 between reorganization energy λ and Stokes shift 2λ; factor 2/π between the Ohmic friction coefficient η and the dimensionless Kondo/coupling parameter α. Rates in the Marcus/golden-rule regime depend on λ inside exp[−(ΔG+λ)²/4λk_BT], so a factor-2 error in λ moves the activation term by (ΔG+λ)²/4λ − (ΔG+2λ)²/8λ, easily tens of k_BT.
gaps.example: Caldeira–Leggett/Weiss: J(ω) = (π/2)Σ_k (c_k²/m_kω_k) δ(ω−ω_k), λ = (1/π)∫₀^∞ dω J(ω)/ω, Ohmic form J(ω) = (π/2)αω e^{−ω/ω_c}. Chemical-physics variant: J̃(ω) = Σ_k (c_k²/2m_kω_k) δ(ω−ω_k) = J(ω)/π, λ = ∫₀^∞ dω J̃(ω)/ω, Ohmic form J̃(ω) = ηω with η = (π/2)α (ħ=1). Both are printed as 'the spectral density J(ω)'.
gaps.fingerprint: The printed definition of J in terms of c_k (presence/absence of π/2); the printed λ integral (1/π vs 2/π vs no prefactor); whether the Ohmic parameter is called η (friction, dimensionful) or α (Kondo, dimensionless); whether the quantity relating J to the correlation function carries coth(βħω/2) or 2/(1−e^{−βħω}); the phrase 'Stokes shift' used interchangeably with 'reorganization energy'.

gaps.name: Symmetry numbers vs reaction-path degeneracy in transition-state-theory rate expressions
gaps.what_breaks: The combinatorial prefactor of a TST rate constant can be carried either by rotational symmetry numbers σ inside every partition function or by an explicit reaction-path degeneracy L‡ multiplying a σ-free expression — never both. Papers print both styles with the same symbol k and the same units (cm³ molecule⁻¹ s⁻¹), and the prefactor is exactly dimensionless, so no dimensional check can detect double counting or omission. Chiral transition states add a further factor of 2 (both enantiomeric TS structures contribute) that is conventionally folded into σ by some authors and stated separately by others, and internal-rotation symmetry numbers are handled inconsistently again.
gaps.magnitude: Integer, typically 2–12, occasionally larger; the chiral-TS factor is exactly 2. For CH₄ + H → CH₃ + H₂: σ(CH₄) = 12, σ(TS) = 3, so σ_react/σ_TS = 4, exactly the reaction-path degeneracy — applying both gives a rate too large by 4.
gaps.example: Style A: k = (k_BT/h)(Q‡/Q_{CH₄}Q_H) e^{−ΔV‡/k_BT} with Q_rot = (1/σ)(…)^{3/2}, σ(CH₄)=12, σ(TS)=3, σ(H₂)=2. Style B: k = L‡ (k_BT/h)(Q̃‡/Q̃_{CH₄}Q̃_H) e^{−ΔV‡/k_BT} with all σ set to 1 and L‡ = 4 (four equivalent hydrogens).
gaps.fingerprint: σ appearing inside Q_rot AND a separate factor named L, L‡, n, g, or 'reaction path degeneracy' in the same rate expression ⇒ double count. Absence of both ⇒ omission. The phrases 'symmetry number', 'reaction path degeneracy', 'the two mirror-image transition states', and a table of σ values per species are the anchors.

gaps.name: Stoichiometric factor in rate-law definitions (rate of reaction vs rate of species loss; the self-reaction 2)
gaps.what_breaks: For a reaction with stoichiometric coefficient ν ≠ 1 in the rate-determining species, k defined through the IUPAC rate of reaction v = (1/ν_B) d[B]/dt differs by exactly ν from k defined through the species loss rate −d[A]/dt. Both are 'k', both have identical units, and both appear in modern evaluated databases and papers. Nothing dimensional distinguishes them; the equations differ only by a dimensionless integer that lives in a prose definition sentence.
gaps.magnitude: Exactly the stoichiometric coefficient — factor 2 for the ubiquitous radical self-reactions (HO₂+HO₂, CH₃+CH₃, R+R), factor 3 for rarer cases.
gaps.example: Variant A (rate-of-reaction basis): −d[HO₂]/dt = 2k[HO₂]². Variant B (loss-rate basis): −d[HO₂]/dt = k′[HO₂]², with k′ = 2k. Both are reported as 'the HO₂ self-reaction rate constant' in cm³ molecule⁻¹ s⁻¹, and the two numbers differ by exactly a factor of 2.
gaps.fingerprint: The reaction as written contains a species with stoichiometric coefficient ≠ 1 on the side it is consumed from (i.e. '2A → …' or 'A + A → …'); then check whether that coefficient appears in the printed ODE, and whether the defining sentence says 'rate of reaction' (IUPAC, coefficient divided out) or 'rate of disappearance/loss of A'.

gaps.name: Anharmonic constant conventions: sign of ω_e x_e vs x_ij, and off-diagonal double counting
gaps.what_breaks: The diatomic (Herzberg) vibrational expansion carries the anharmonicity with an explicit minus sign, so tabulated ω_e x_e is positive; the polyatomic/VPT2 convention absorbs the sign into the matrix element, so x_11 = −ω_e x_e is negative. Separately, the cross terms are written either as a restricted sum over i ≤ j or as an unrestricted double sum with a ½, which changes every off-diagonal x_ij by a factor 2. Both variants are printed in cm⁻¹ and both are dimensionally perfect, so a units tool comparing 'the anharmonic constants' across a diatomic paper and a polyatomic VPT2 paper silently compares numbers of opposite sign or twice the size.
gaps.magnitude: Sign flip on diagonal terms; factor 2 on off-diagonal terms. Concretely for H₂: ω_e = 4401.21 cm⁻¹, ω_e x_e = +121.33 cm⁻¹ (Herzberg) ⇔ x_11 = −121.33 cm⁻¹ (matrix convention).
gaps.example: Diatomic: G(v) = ω_e(v+½) − ω_e x_e (v+½)² + ω_e y_e (v+½)³. Polyatomic: G(v) = Σ_i ω_i(v_i + d_i/2) + Σ_{i≤j} x_ij (v_i + d_i/2)(v_j + d_j/2), which for a diatomic gives x_11 = −ω_e x_e; the unrestricted-sum variant writes ½Σ_i Σ_j x̄_ij(…)(…) with x̄_ij = x_ij for i≠j but x̄_ii = 2x_ii.
gaps.fingerprint: Sign in front of the quadratic term; whether the anharmonicity is written as the single product token 'ω_e x_e' (Herzberg) or as an indexed matrix x_ij; whether the double sum is restricted (i ≤ j) or free with a ½ prefactor; presence of the vibrational degeneracy d_i/2 (polyatomic convention marker).

gaps.name: Watson A- vs S-reduced effective rotational Hamiltonians (Δ_J, δ_J vs D_J, d_1, d_2)
gaps.what_breaks: Quartic and sextic centrifugal-distortion constants are parameters of two unitarily inequivalent reduced Hamiltonians. Δ_J and D_J play the same role, are both reported in MHz or kHz, and are frequently both written 'D_J' in prose — but they are numerically different, are entered into fitting programs with different fixed signs, and a set from one reduction is not usable in the other. A units/dimension tool sees a perfectly consistent MHz-valued parameter either way and will happily 'translate' between papers that are not comparable. The choice of axis representation (I^r, I^l, III^l) compounds this.
gaps.magnitude: No universal factor: the A↔S differences are of the order of the constants themselves (e.g. Δ_J = D_J − 2d_2, and |d_2| can exceed |D_J|, so Δ_J > 0 is compatible with D_J < 0). Predicted line positions shift by MHz — orders of magnitude beyond the kHz precision such papers claim. Sign conventions also differ: Pickett's SPFIT enters the quartic terms as −Δ_J, −Δ_JK, −Δ_K, −δ_J, −δ_K in the A reduction and −D_J, −D_JK, −D_K, +d_1, +d_2 in the S reduction.
gaps.example: A reduction: H = H_rot − Δ_J J⁴ − Δ_JK J²J_z² − Δ_K J_z⁴ − 2δ_J J²(J_x²−J_y²) − δ_K{J_z², J_x²−J_y²}. S reduction: H = H_rot − D_J J⁴ − D_JK J²J_z² − D_K J_z⁴ + d_1 J²(J_+²+J_−²) + d_2 (J_+⁴+J_−⁴). Both fit the same spectrum and both are captioned 'quartic centrifugal distortion constants (MHz)'.
gaps.fingerprint: Symbol set {Δ_J, Δ_JK, Δ_K, δ_J, δ_K} ⇒ A reduction; {D_J, D_JK, D_K, d_1, d_2} ⇒ S reduction; explicit 'A reduction'/'S reduction' and representation labels I^r / I^l / III^l; the presence of the J_+⁴+J_−⁴ operator (S only) or the {J_z², J_x²−J_y²} anticommutator (A only).

gaps.name: Isotopologue-abundance weighting in tabulated line intensities (HITRAN-style S)
gaps.what_breaks: HITRAN and its derivatives report line intensity S already multiplied by the natural terrestrial isotopic abundance of the isotopologue, so S is an intensity per molecule of the *bulk gas*, not per molecule of that isotopologue. Line-by-line calculations for enriched, depleted, or extraterrestrial samples, and any comparison against an ab initio per-molecule intensity, need the abundance divided out. The units are identical either way — cm⁻¹/(molecule cm⁻²) — so no dimensional or unit check can see the missing factor.
gaps.magnitude: 1/IA, where IA is the tabulated abundance: 0.984204 for ¹²C¹⁶O₂ (0.16%), 0.011057 for ¹³C¹⁶O₂ (factor 90), 3.1069×10⁻⁴ for HD¹⁶O (factor 3219). Errors of three to four orders of magnitude for minor isotopologues.
gaps.example: Variant A (HITRAN convention): S = 1.0×10⁻²³ cm⁻¹/(molecule cm⁻²) for an HDO line, i.e. per molecule of total water. Variant B (per-isotopologue, as an ab initio line list or an enriched-sample retrieval would state it): S = 3.22×10⁻²⁰ cm⁻¹/(molecule cm⁻²) for the same transition.
gaps.fingerprint: Unit string 'cm⁻¹/(molecule·cm⁻²)' together with a reference temperature of 296 K and a HITRAN/HITEMP/GEISA citation or a molecule/isotopologue ID pair; conversely, an ab initio line list or an 'isotopically pure' sample statement signals the unweighted convention. Also flag the older band-strength unit cm⁻² atm⁻¹, which additionally folds in a reference temperature and pressure.

found.overall: This field is not well covered by the current design, but the misses are of a specific type: the engine is built around dimensionful generators and unit-system riders, while quantum chemistry and molecular spectroscopy are wrecked mainly by (a) dimensionless combinatorial prefactors that live in a prose definition (symmetry numbers vs reaction-path degeneracy, stoichiometric 2 in self-reaction rate laws, the ½ in the Buckingham quadrupole, the π/2 in a bath spectral density), (b) same-symbol-different-operational-definition parameters where the two variants are equally dimensionally sound and even equally unit-labelled (Watson A vs S reduction, Herzberg ω_e x_e vs VPT2 x_11, HITRAN abundance-weighted S), and (c) a small set of definitions whose variants actually change dimension, which will make the lint report a false error rather than stay silent (Einstein B on an energy-density vs intensity basis; polarizability as a volume in esu). Of these, the highest-leverage single addition is not a registry row at all but the schema feature in gap 5: a rule for suppressed reference-state divisors inside logs, plus the requirement that fitted intercepts co-transform when the argument's units are converted. Without it the tool false-positives on nearly every kinetics and thermochemistry paper it reads, and — worse — its own unit conversions of Arrhenius and Antoine parameters will be internally inconsistent while passing every dimensional check it performs. The two structural entries (two-electron integral index pairing, Watson reductions) are the ones where the right answer is to refuse or tag rather than translate.

verdict.lens: Quantum chemistry / molecular spectroscopy: electronic-structure integral notation, molecular moments and response tensors, rovibrational effective Hamiltonians, radiative-transition coefficients, TST statistical prefactors, system–bath models.

verdicts.gap: Einstein B-coefficient radiation-field basis (ρ_ν vs ρ_ω vs ρ_ν̃ vs mean intensity J̄_ν)
verdicts.notes: Recomputed and all four A–B relations check out: ρ_ν basis A=8πhν³/c³·B_ρ with [B_ρ]=m³J⁻¹s⁻²; mean-intensity basis A=2hν³/c²·B_J with [B_J]=m²·sr·J⁻¹s⁻¹, since u_ν=(4π/c)J̄_ν ⇒ B_J=(4π/c)B_ρ; ρ_ω basis B_ω=2πB_ν ⇒ A=ħω³/(π²c³)·B_ω; wavenumber basis B_ν̃=B_ν/c ⇒ A=8πhcν̃³·B_ν̃. NUMERIC CORRECTION: 4π/c = 4.19×10⁻⁸ s m⁻¹; the quoted 4.19×10⁻¹⁰ is the cgs value (s cm⁻¹). Same slip in the compounded figure: c/2 = 1.5×10⁸ m s⁻¹, not 1.5×10¹⁰ (that is cm s⁻¹). SCOPE TRIM: the ν↔ω leg duplicates exclusion 2 ('per-Hz vs per-(rad/s)') and the existing registry row 'h vs ħ / ν vs ω'; the genuinely new content is the ρ_ν vs J̄_ν vs I_ν basis, which is dimension-changing. TREATMENT: that dimension-changing leg is not a dimensionless rider — it needs a quantity-kind tag plus a ×4π/c converter edge (and an sr in the dimension vector or an explicit steradian-bookkeeping decision); only the ν/ν̃/ω leg is rider-shaped.

verdicts.gap: Two-electron integral index pairing: chemists' (Mulliken) vs physicists' (Dirac) vs antisymmetrized notation
verdicts.notes: Identities verified: (pq|rs)=⟨pr|qs⟩; ⟨pq||rs⟩=⟨pq|rs⟩−⟨pq|sr⟩; the printed RHF Fock expression F_μν=h_μν+Σ_λσ P_λσ[(μν|λσ)−½(μλ|νσ)] and the spin-orbital f_pq=h_pq+Σ_i⟨pi||qi⟩ are both correct as written. Not in coverage or exclusions (exclusion 1 is QFT state normalization; exclusion 4 is differential-form/Levi-Civita bookkeeping). Two refinements the entry should carry: (i) the double-bar form is an expansion into two terms, not a relabeling, so it must be rewritten before any per-integral mapping; (ii) the '−½' in the Mulliken RHF expression comes from spin summation over a spatial-orbital density, not from the notation fork — an entry that files it under 'Mulliken exchange prefactor' will mis-translate a UHF/spin-orbital paper. Following the round-2 sign-axis pattern (mechanical rewrite + tag) is the right shape; note this is index-structure parsing, which is a genuine scope extension beyond dimensional solving.

verdicts.gap: Molecular multipole moment definition: Buckingham ½-traceless Θ vs untraced second moment vs unhalved Q
verdicts.notes: Conventions and conversions verified: Θ_αβ=½Σq_i(3r_αr_β−r²δ_αβ) (Buckingham/IUPAC); 1 D·Å = 1 buckingham = 10⁻²⁶ esu cm² = 3.3356×10⁻⁴⁰ C m²; 1 e a₀² = 4.4866×10⁻⁴⁰ C m² = 1.3451 D·Å; Θ_zz=(3/2)M_zz−½Tr M. Gaussian does print both a primitive and a traceless quadrupole block, so the three-way fork is real in practice. Two corrections: (i) the primitive↔traceless map is linear, not affine, and it requires all three diagonal components — from a single reported component it is non-invertible, so that leg must refuse rather than convert; (ii) missing sub-fork worth folding in: origin dependence (center of mass vs center of nuclear charge vs a specified origin), which matters for charged or dipolar species and is exactly as invisible to a dimensional check.

verdicts.gap: Molecular response tensors α, β, γ: order-dependent (4πε₀) rider and polarizability-as-volume
verdicts.notes: Rule verified from q_G = q_SI/√(4πε₀), E_G = √(4πε₀)E_SI: α_SI=(4πε₀)α_G, β_SI=(4πε₀)^{3/2}β_G, γ_SI=(4πε₀)²γ_G, i.e. (4πε₀)^{(n+1)/2} ✓. CODATA a.u. values all check: α 1.6487772×10⁻⁴¹ C²m²J⁻¹ = 0.1481847 Å³; β 3.2063613×10⁻⁵³ C³m³J⁻²; γ 6.2353800×10⁻⁶⁵ C⁴m⁴J⁻³; α(H₂O) 1.45 Å³ × 4πε₀ = 1.61×10⁻⁴⁰ C²m²J⁻¹ ✓; exponent-off-by-one = 1.11×10⁻¹⁰ ✓. Confidence should be 'certain', not 'likely'. TREATMENT REFINEMENT: do not add one rider row per tensor order — the exponent is (net power of e in the symbol)/2, so a single charge-power-keyed rider covers α, β, γ and also μ, magnetizability, molecular χ⁽ⁿ⁾, etc. Also flag that the entry silently assumes the Taylor (B) convention μ=μ₀+αE+½βE²+⅙γE³; the no-factorial (T) convention differs by 2 on β and 6 on γ, and that leg belongs with exclusion 3's degeneracy-factor family, not here.

verdicts.gap: Suppressed standard-state divisor inside transcendental functions, and the co-transform of fitted intercepts
verdicts.notes: Strongest item in the set. Arithmetic verified: cm³ molecule⁻¹s⁻¹ → L mol⁻¹s⁻¹ multiplies by N_A/1000 = 6.0221×10²⁰; ln = 47.85, log₁₀ = 20.78 ✓. log₁₀(750.062) = 2.8751 ✓. Both water Antoine sets are the standard NIST ones (8.07131/1730.63/233.426 in mmHg,°C; 4.6543/1435.264/−64.848 in bar,K) ✓ — but note they are independent fits over different ranges, so 8.07131−2.8751 = 5.196 ≠ 4.6543; the tool must not 'verify' one against the other, only co-transform within a single fit. Not a duplicate: the logarithmic refuse class covers quantities that are inherently log-defined (dB, dex, pH), the decadic/Napierian row covers absorption coefficients, and the RT ln 24.46 row fixes the standard state's *value* — none of them supply the lint rule (dimensionful argument under a log = suppressed reference, not an error) or the intercept co-transform, which is the part that silently corrupts data while passing every dimensional check.

verdicts.gap: Bath spectral-density and reorganization-energy normalization in system–bath models
verdicts.notes: Core fork verified and self-consistent: J(ω)=(π/2)Σ_k(c_k²/m_kω_k)δ(ω−ω_k) with λ=(1/π)∫J/ω dω = Σ_k c_k²/(2m_kω_k²); the chemical-physics J̃ = J/π with λ=∫J̃/ω dω gives the same λ ✓. Stokes shift = 2λ ✓. THREE CORRECTIONS: (i) η and α are not related by a bare 2/π — in the Caldeira–Leggett→spin-boson mapping α = ηq₀²/(2πħ), so the relation carries the tunneling distance q₀²; the π-only statement holds only after q₀ and ħ are set to 1, which the entry must say or it will mis-translate. (ii) Marcus magnitude is exaggerated: at ΔG=0, using 2λ for λ changes the barrier by λ/4 ≈ 0.125–0.25 eV for λ = 0.5–1 eV, i.e. ~5–10 k_BT at 300 K (still a 10⁴ rate error), not 'tens of k_BT' — that would need λ ≳ 3 eV. (iii) Trim the coth(βħω/2) vs 2/(1−e^{−βħω}) leg: that is the quantum one-sided/two-sided correlation-function question already inside exclusion 2. Remaining new content — the π/2 in the microscopic c_k sum and λ vs Stokes shift — is genuinely uncovered.

verdicts.gap: Symmetry numbers vs reaction-path degeneracy in transition-state-theory rate expressions
verdicts.notes: Physics is right: for CH₄+H→CH₃+H₂, σ(CH₄)σ(H)/σ(TS) = 12·1/3 = 4 = L‡ exactly, so carrying both overcounts by 4; the chiral-TS factor 2 and inconsistent internal-rotation σ are real (Pollak–Pechukas; Fernández-Ramos et al. 2007). But it is mis-slotted as a new_axis. This is a single dimensionless integer fork with a prose fingerprint — precisely what the existing 21-row dimensionless-conventions registry is for — plus a double-count lint rule ('σ inside Q_rot AND a separate L/L‡/n/g in the same expression'). A new axis buys nothing, because the tool cannot compute σ or L‡ without the point groups of reactant and transition state, which it does not have: it can detect double counting or omission, never supply the missing factor. Correct slot: registry_entry + lint, v2 (tier is fine).

verdicts.gap: Stoichiometric factor in rate-law definitions (rate of reaction vs rate of species loss; the self-reaction 2)
verdicts.notes: Verified: IUPAC rate of reaction v = (1/ν_B)d[B]/dt, so for A+A→products, −d[A]/dt = 2v = 2k_IUPAC[A]², giving k_loss = 2k_IUPAC exactly as claimed. The HO₂+HO₂ example is the canonical one and evaluated databases (IUPAC, JPL/NASA) do print the defining ODE precisely because of this ambiguity. Not in coverage or exclusions; dimensionally invisible (identical units both ways). registry_entry at v2 is the right slot. Only refinement: the fingerprint should also catch the case where the coefficient is absorbed into a tabulated k with no ODE printed at all — then the honest output is a flag, not a factor.

verdicts.gap: Anharmonic constant conventions: sign of ω_e x_e vs x_ij, and off-diagonal double counting
verdicts.notes: The sign fork is real and correctly stated: Herzberg G(v)=ω_e(v+½)−ω_e x_e(v+½)²+ω_e y_e(v+½)³ with tabulated ω_e x_e positive, vs the VPT2 matrix element x_11 = −ω_e x_e; H₂ numbers ✓ (ω_e = 4401.21, ω_e x_e = 121.33 cm⁻¹). The double-counting leg is misattributed. CORRECTED CLAIM: with the pairing the entry itself writes (restricted Σ_{i≤j}x_ij vs unrestricted ½Σ_iΣ_j x̄_ij), its own relations x̄_ij = x_ij (i≠j), x̄_ii = 2x_ii show the DIAGONAL constants double while the off-diagonals are unchanged — the opposite of the headline 'changes every off-diagonal x_ij by a factor 2'. The off-diagonal factor 2 arises only against a third variant, the unrestricted Σ_iΣ_j written without the ½. Keep the entry, but enumerate all three sum conventions and attach the factor to the right elements, or the tool will introduce the error it is meant to catch.

verdicts.gap: Watson A- vs S-reduced effective rotational Hamiltonians (Δ_J, δ_J vs D_J, d_1, d_2)
verdicts.notes: The fork is real, uncovered, and worth an entry: the two reductions are unitarily inequivalent parameterizations, the symbol sets and operator fingerprints given are correct (J_+⁴+J_−⁴ is S-only; the {J_z², J_x²−J_y²} anticommutator is A-only), Δ_J = D_J − 2d_2 is the standard Watson relation, and the I^r/I^l/III^l representation label really is required metadata. Three over-reaches to correct: (a) 'A↔S differences are of the order of the constants themselves' — for the leading quartic constants the difference is 2d_2, typically a small percentage of D_J for near-symmetric tops; it becomes large only for strongly asymmetric species and for the sextic set. (b) '|d_2| can exceed |D_J|, so Δ_J > 0 is compatible with D_J < 0' is not a realistic case — D_J is positive for essentially every fitted molecule; drop this illustration. (c) refuse_class is too strong: exact Watson transformations between COMPLETE A and S parameter sets exist, so the correct treatment is detect-and-tag (the Euclidean-continuation pattern), refusing only partial sets and cross-reduction mixing. The practical warning — never mix sets, MHz-level prediction errors against kHz-precision claims — survives intact.

verdicts.gap: Isotopologue-abundance weighting in tabulated line intensities (HITRAN-style S)
verdicts.notes: All numbers check against HITRAN's abundance table: ¹²C¹⁶O₂ (626) 0.984204; ¹³C¹⁶O₂ (636) 0.011057 → ×90.4; HD¹⁶O (162) 3.10693×10⁻⁴ → ×3219; 1.0×10⁻²³/3.1069×10⁻⁴ = 3.22×10⁻²⁰ ✓; unit string cm⁻¹/(molecule·cm⁻²) at 296 K ✓. Genuinely uncovered and dimensionally invisible. One coupling note: this is an instance of exclusion 5's quantity-kind tagging (identical unit string, different quantity — per bulk-gas molecule vs per isotopologue molecule), so it should be built as a kind tag plus an abundance data table rather than as a free-standing converter class; the converter edge is then just ×1/IA keyed to the molecule/isotopologue ID pair. The secondary flag on the older band-strength unit cm⁻² atm⁻¹ is correct and does need its own reference T and P (Loschmidt-number) metadata.

verdict.overall: Adjudication: 8 confirmed, 1 wrong_treatment, 2 overstated, 0 not-real, 0 duplicates. This is an unusually strong batch — the lens is right that the engine's dimensionful-generator core is orthogonal to the three failure modes named, and none of the eleven collapses into the coverage summary or the round-3 exclusion list on inspection. Ranking by leverage I agree with the critic on gap 5 (suppressed reference divisor + fitted-intercept co-transform) as the single highest-value addition: it is the only one that both false-positives on a large literature and silently corrupts data while passing every check the tool performs. Next are gap 3 (multipole definitions, with the origin-dependence sub-fork added) and gap 11 (HITRAN abundance weighting), both cheap data entries with large numeric consequences. Systematic defects across the batch, for the parent to apply before implementation: (1) magnitude figures are quoted in cgs while labelled SI in gap 1 — 4π/c is 4.19×10⁻⁸ s m⁻¹, not 4.19×10⁻¹⁰, and the compounded ratio is 1.5×10⁸, not 1.5×10¹⁰; (2) two entries mis-attribute which elements a factor lands on or which parameter carries a length scale — gap 9's factor 2 falls on the diagonal constants, not the off-diagonals, in the pairing the entry itself writes down, and gap 6's η↔α relation carries q₀²/ħ, not a bare 2/π; (3) two treatments are mis-slotted — gap 7 is a dimensionless-registry row plus a double-count lint, not a new axis (the tool can never supply σ or L‡, only detect double counting), and gap 10 should be detect-and-tag rather than a blanket refuse, since exact Watson transformations exist for complete parameter sets; (4) three entries need scope trims where they graze the exclusion list — gap 1's ν↔ω leg, gap 6's coth-vs-Bose correlation-function leg, and gap 4's ½β/⅙γ Taylor-convention leg all belong to already-identified families and should not be re-litigated inside these rows. Two rate-magnitude claims are softer than stated: the Marcus λ-doubling error is ~5–10 k_BT for realistic λ, not tens, and A↔S reduction differences in the leading quartic constants are typically percent-level rather than order-unity. Finally, gap 4's rider should be implemented once as a charge-power-keyed rule, exponent = (net power of e)/2, rather than as per-tensor-order rows.
